items.title: Libraries Run Rust Inside Python (With PyO3)
items.summary_zh: 教程梳理PyO3/maturin把Rust扩展送进pip生态；simonw关心Pyodide兼容，现多已有WASM构建。逾50赞。

quotes.author: simonw
quotes.en:
I was a bit nervous about this trend when it started picking up because I care about Pyodide (Python running via WebAssembly) and libraries that use PyO3 might not work in Pyodide.
Thankfully that's now been mostly solved - you can compile and publish WASM builds of Rust or C extensions on PyPI now and a Pyodide can then use them.
Here's the WASM build of the Rust-including Pydantic-core package for example: https://pypi.org/project/pydantic_core/#pydantic_core-2.49.0-cp314-cp314-pyemscripten_2026_0_wasm32.whl
quotes.zh: 这趋势刚起时我有点紧张，因为我在意Pyodide（Wasm上的Python），用PyO3的库可能跑不了。幸好现已大体解决——可以编译发布Rust/C扩展的WASM构建。

quotes.author: the__alchemist
quotes.en: This is a nice party trick! I use it to provide easy installation of software that is written in rust, but is primarily used by Python users. (e.g.: Biology tools) They can do `pip install `, since some people prefer this over downloading executables/installers. Bonus: Maturin/PyO3 can build "manylinux" binaries automatically, which helps with the Linux ABI diaspora.
quotes.zh: 挺好的“表演技巧”！我用它让主要Rust写的、却由Python用户使用的软件（如生物工具）能`pip install`，有人更喜欢这样而不是下安装包。

items.title: Base84 deserves a place in file names
items.title_zh: Base84该在文件名里有一席之地
items.summary_zh: 博文主张用更短字母表编码文件名；评论区吐槽特殊字符会让shell与agent转义翻车，Base62往往够用。逾50赞。

quotes.author: abound
quotes.en:
> Here’s the alphabet, in encoding order:
> ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789!#$%&'()+,-;=@[]^_`{}~
Yeah I definitely don't want any of those last ~22 characters in file names if I need to do anything with them from a shell
quotes.zh: 字母表编码顺序里那些非字母数字字符——如果还要从shell里摆弄文件名，我绝对不想看到最后那大约22个字符。

quotes.author: bensyverson
quotes.en:
The non-alphanumeric characters are just asking for trouble. Agents will fail to escape them correctly, and the $ could expand a variable.
Base62 (or 64, with -_) is totally sufficient.
quotes.zh: 非字母数字字符就是找麻烦。Agent会转义失败，`$`还可能展开变量。Base62（或带- _的64）完全够用。

items.title: On Binary Translation and Its Consequences
items.title_zh: 论二进制翻译及其后果
items.summary_zh: Chips and Cheese长文谈二进制翻译与微架构冗余；Rosetta 2作者现身，用户回忆M1上JIT例外。近50赞。

quotes.author: cwzwarich
quotes.en:
[Disclaimer: I wrote Rosetta 2, so everything I say is biased by that.]
Contemporary out-of-order CPUs are incredibly over-provisioned; microarchitects will justify a new feature by another 0.1% gain on some benchmark. The end result is a CPU that's pretty decent at handling the sort of code bloat that comes from a binary translator.
There's also a big tradeoff in adding more optimizations to a binary translator. You would like to be able to precisely handle exceptions (especially ones caused by invalid memory accesses) while presenting a userspace exception handler with an architecturally valid state for the source program. There are some optimizations that would be easy to do in principle but are painful for maintaining this mapping between source program states and translated program states. The complexity burden combined with the difficulty of debugging that added complexity (or exhaustively verifying it up-front) shapes many of your decisions when writing a production binary translator. You should always have more Cool (tm) ideas than you actually use in practice.
quotes.zh: 【声明：我写了Rosetta 2，以下有偏见。】当代乱序CPU冗余得不可思议；微架构师常靠基准上再抠0.1%证明新特性。结果是CPU很擅长处理翻译器制造的“怪异”代码。

quotes.author: torginus
quotes.en: When I bought my M1 Macbook, I had a firsthand experience with how well binary translation worked. It was almost perfect with one MAJOR exception - anything that used JIT - so stuff like Electron apps or Java stuff (IntelliJ-based IDEs). Which was kinda ironic - JITs were designed around the idea of portability across CPU architectures, yet usually they are one of the hardest pieces of code to port, and they make this sort of binary translation approach - which has relatively long compile times but good exec time - very  slow and painful.
quotes.zh: 买M1 MacBook时我亲身体会二进制翻译有多好——几乎完美，除了一个大例外：用JIT的东西，比如Electron或Java（IntelliJ系IDE）。挺讽刺，JIT本就是为性能设计的。

items.title: Cpak – OCI application package format for Linux desktops, servers and devices
items.title_zh: Cpak：面向Linux桌面/服务器/设备的OCI应用打包格式
items.summary_zh: 新格式复用Dockerfile结构、无守护进程、强调轻量去重；评论形容“像Docker但更轻”，也有人吐槽文档味像Claude。逾40赞。

quotes.author: nine_k
quotes.en:
In short: structurally like Docker (reuses Dockerfiles), but without a daemon, and, unlike Podman or Nix, very lightweight, only two binaries do everything.
Common chunks of data are shared / deduplicated across installed packages, again like Docker or Nix.
The runtime is under LGPL2.
quotes.zh: 简言之：结构上像Docker（复用Dockerfile），但无守护进程；又不像Podman或Nix那么重，两个二进制就能搞定。公共数据块在已装包之间共享/去重，也像Docker或Nix。

quotes.author: stephenlf
quotes.en:
> Follow a complete course, change real manifests and see what cpak accepts, refuses or changes. Professional paths lead to an exam and a public, verifiable credential.
Holy Claude
quotes.zh: “跟完一整门课、改真实manifest，看cpak接受、拒绝或改写什么。职业路径通向考试与可公开核验的证书。”——好家伙，很Claude。
